questions.question: Choose the incorrect option regarding the Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) operationalised by RBI in 2021.
options: To benefit the acquiring banks/non-banks and merchants by lowering overall acceptance infrastructure costs.
To increase payments acceptance infrastructure by adding 30 lakh touch points every year - 10 lakh physical and 20 lakh digital payment acceptance devices.
RBI has contributed Rs 250 crore to this fund.
To increase the number of acceptance devices multi-fold in the country.
POS will be established in tier 1 and tier 2 cities
questions.explanation: The PIDF targets deployment of payment acceptance infrastructure in tier-3 to tier-6 centres and north-eastern states, not tier 1 and tier 2 cities - so that statement is incorrect. The RBI made an initial contribution of Rs 250 crore to the Rs 345 crore corpus.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) launched recurring payments for UPI. What is its name?
questions.explanation: NPCI launched 'UPI AutoPay' for recurring payments, letting customers set e-mandates for subscriptions, EMIs and bills through UPI.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: In December 2020, SBI Cards and Payment Services Ltd (SBI Card) raised how many rupees (in crores) by issuing bonds on a private placement basis?
questions.explanation: SBI Card raised Rs 550 crore in December 2020 through the issue of non-convertible debentures on a private placement basis.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: According to RBI's National Strategy for Financial Inclusion, the minimum radius within which banking facilities should be available to a person is ______.
questions.explanation: The National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (2019-2024) targets access to formal banking services within a 5 km radius of every village/hamlet.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Indian traditional mathematics 'Kotipakoti' has how many zeros?
questions.explanation: In traditional Indian numeration, kotipakoti denotes 10^21, i.e. a number with 21 zeros.
